title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Alps and eating with them
objectives: Pair the region's wines with food

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Alto Adige labels are often bilingual: Alto Adige or Südtirol, Pinot Grigio or Ruländer, Lagrein or Lagrein Dunkel. Most wines are varietal, named by grape. Trentino labels name the grape or Trentodoc. Kellerei or Cantina means a winery, often a co-operative.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: The region's food blends Italian and Austrian: speck, smoked ham; canederli, bread dumplings; strudel; polenta; and mountain cheeses. Pinot Bianco and Pinot Grigio suit speck and light dishes; Gewürztraminer suits spicy food and cheese; Lagrein suits game, goulash and grilled meat; Trentodoc suits aperitifs and fried food.

steps.prompt: Which wine suits speck and light dishes?
steps.explanation: A crisp Alpine white suits the smoky ham.

steps.body: Try Lagrein with goulash, a dish of Austrian heritage still common in Alto Adige.

steps.prompt: Most Alto Adige wines are named by grape.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels are often bilingual and varietal
Pinot Bianco suits speck; Lagrein suits game
